body_md: Yew is React-like for Rust: function components, hooks like `use_state`, and html! macro. It compiles to WASM and updates DOM efficiently. Best when your team thinks in components.

quiz.explain: Yew mirrors React component and hook patterns.
options: Yew uses function components plus html! macro

takeaway: Choose Yew for component-style WASM UIs.
trap: Cloning state handles in every closure without need.

body_md: Leptos uses fine-grained reactivity: signals update only dependent DOM nodes, no virtual DOM diff. `create_signal` plus `<Show>` keeps large pages fast with tiny binaries.
code:
let (count, set_count) = create_signal(0);
view! { <button on:click=move |_| set_count(count()+1)>{count}</button> }

quiz.explain: Signals track dependencies and patch precisely.
quiz.q: How does Leptos update the DOM?

takeaway: Use signals for surgical DOM updates.
trap: Nesting effects that trigger cascading updates.

body_md: Dioxus targets web, desktop, and mobile from one RSX codebase. Write `rsx!` once, run in browser WASM or native WebView. Ideal for FerrisFeed demos across platforms.

quiz.explain: Dioxus renders RSX to web/desktop/mobile backends.

takeaway: Pick Dioxus for multi-target Rust UIs.
trap: Assuming all native plugins exist on web target.

body_md: Hello app flow: `trunk serve` builds Yew/Leptos, bundles wasm, and hot-reloads. Point trunk at index.html, add `#[wasm_bindgen(start)]` or main, and iterate in milliseconds.
code:
cargo install trunk
trunk serve --open
# edits rebuild wasm instantly
hook: trunk serve is your dev loop.

quiz.explain: Trunk is the WASM web bundler and dev server.
options: Trunk builds and serves WASM web apps
quiz.q: How do you run Yew or Leptos locally?

takeaway: Serve with trunk for fast rebuilds.
trap: Forgetting trunk config for asset paths.

body_md: Embed live WASM demo in a WebView: load local `index.html` that inits pkg, expose a JS bridge for theme and data, and lazy-load on scroll into view. Keep bridge JSON-serializable.
hook: Live demo inside the lesson itself.

quiz.explain: Local assets plus message bridge enable offline interactive demos.
options: Load local bundle plus message bridge
quiz.q: How do you run a live WASM demo via WebView?

takeaway: Bundle demo locally and message across the bridge.
trap: Allowing remote URLs in demo WebView weakens sandbox.

body_md: State patterns: Yew uses `use_reducer`, Leptos uses signals plus stores, Dioxus uses `use_state`. Lift shared state to context providers, not prop drilling, and derive UI from one source.
hook: One source of truth, three flavors.

quiz.explain: Central signals/stores prevent divergent UI copies.
quiz.q: How should framework state be managed?

takeaway: Centralize state and derive views from it.
trap: Mutating props directly breaks reactivity tracking.

body_md: Routing: `yew-router`, `leptos_router`, `dioxus-router` map URLs to components. Define routes as enums, link with components not anchors, and lazy-load heavy pages as separate wasm chunks.
hook: Enums as URLs — routing without strings.

quiz.explain: Typed routes prevent broken links at compile time.
options: Typed route enums with router components
quiz.q: How do Rust WASM frameworks route?

takeaway: Model routes as types for safe navigation.
trap: Full page reloads that discard WASM state.

body_md: Fetch in frameworks via async resources: Leptos `create_resource`, Yew `use_effect_with` plus fetch, Dioxus `use_future`. Show skeletons while pending and cache by key to avoid refetch storms.

quiz.explain: Resources tie async fetch lifecycle to reactivity.
options: Resources bind fetch to reactive lifecycle
quiz.q: How do you load server data in Leptos?

takeaway: Use resources/futures for cancellable async UI.
trap: Fetching on every render without memoization.

body_md: Test with `wasm-bindgen-test` in headless browsers. Unit-test logic natively, then run `--headless --chrome` for DOM tests. Mock fetch with stub responses to keep CI fast.
code:
cargo install wasm-pack
wasm-pack test --headless --chrome
# #[wasm_bindgen_test] marks tests

quiz.explain: wasm-pack test drives real browser engines.
options: Run wasm-bindgen tests headless in browsers
quiz.q: How do you test framework WASM apps?

takeaway: Split pure logic tests from browser integration tests.
trap: Only testing natively misses DOM glue bugs.

body_md: Choose: Yew for React teams, Leptos for speed and SSR, Dioxus for multi-platform. All interop with JS when needed. Prototype the same todo app in each before committing.
hook: No best framework — only best fit.

quiz.explain: Team shape and targets decide the pick.
options: Match framework to team and targets
quiz.q: How do you pick between Yew, Leptos, and Dioxus?

takeaway: Evaluate against team skills and ship targets.
trap: Rewriting mid-project for hype without measuring.
